correctness.rationale: For κ>1, 0<p<1 and 0≤s≤1, strict monotonicity of the positive 2×2 transmissibility Perron root gives a unique positive threshold. With h=1−τδ, expand F(t)=f(t)[I+δK+O(δ²)] and K=[[-τp,τp],[τ(1−p),q−τ(1−p)]], q=t e^(−t)/f(t). Its simple upper eigenvalue G=(q−τ+sqrt((q−τ)²+4pqτ))/2, yielding t_c=t0−δG/(κ−1)+O(δ²), uniformly for compact τ. Perron derivative at fixed h<1 is p, whereas at h=1 the high-risk diagonal gives t0/(1+δ); the limits differ by 1/p. The leading coefficient B has det(B)=αh≥0, so 1≤tr(B)/rho(B)≤2; equality 2 at α=1,h=1. Independently evaluated exact spectral roots and δ² residuals at four parameter triples using different code; asymptotic and all-parameter proof is analytic, not inferred from finite tests.
